text: sec-bot: [ALERT] potential reflected XSS detected on /embed/preview (query param `src`). scanner=burp-automated severity=high link=https://alerts.internal/1823 Maya: saw the alert. quick repro: payload `` in src shows up in preview iframe and executes. Alex: can repro locally. frontend is doing `innerHTML` on the preview body. looks like this code path is only used for customer trial embeds. Eve: confirmed with minimal curl: `curl -s 'https://app.redwood.ai/embed/preview?src=' | grep onerror` shows the raw string in response. Priya: cc @Maya @Alex - immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback preview feature flag 2) add WAF rule to block `src=` containing `<` 3) temporary CSP to disallow inline scripts on preview frames. Which is fastest? Ben: I can push a WAF rule (Cloudflare) in <10m to block `(<|%3C)` in `src` param. Doing that now. Maya: +1 WAF then feature-flag disable if exploit seen. Also set feature to admin-only until patched. Alex: digging into code. component `PreviewRenderer` sets iframe.contentWindow.document.body.innerHTML = user_html; we'll switch to DOMParser + sanitization. patch ETA 2-3 hrs. Zoe: product question — any customer-facing incidents expected? is any session data leaked to third-party? Maya: so far no evidence of token exfil. the preview iframe is same-origin and doesn't make external requests by default, but payload could create an image beacon. we need to check access logs for odd requests and audit logs for any sensitive endpoints called around the timestamps. Daniel: I'll pull CloudFront logs and WAF logs for the last 24h and run grep for suspicious querystrings. also checking audit logs for any admin API usage that coincides. Eve: quick grep shows 3 requests with payload-like params in the last hour from a single IP (ip: 54.173.22.11). Not sure if attacker or random fuzzing. Ben: WAF rule deployed and blocking ~12 requests/min matching `<` in src param. rule id cf-3847. Priya: good. please also set the preview route to require user to be authenticated and enforce RBAC: only customers with role `tester` or above can use preview until fix. can platform lock that via gateway? Alex: yes I can flip the feature flag to admin-only via flags-service. Doing it now. Ben: feature flag flipped. route returns 403 for non-admins. Maya: escalation: filing an incident ticket (INC-2026) so we track containment, forensics, comms. assign owners for post-incident actions. Zoe: prepping comms: need impact statement and timeline for customers. if we believe no data exfil, we should do a private notice to affected accounts only. Daniel: forensic notes: saving request bodies, headers, and full response content for the suspicious requests. will store in secure S3 bucket with restricted ACL; encryption via KMS key `arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:1111:key/security-forensics`. Priya: ensure the S3 objects have access logged and that only sec-team and oncall can decrypt. confirm KMS key policy includes `sec-eng@redwood.ai` and `platform-sre@redwood.ai`. Daniel: confirmed key policy includes the two. also enabling CloudTrail Data events for the S3 forensic bucket. Eve: patch PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/frontend/pull/724. changes: replace innerHTML with DOMPurify.sanitize + DOMParser. test cases added for common payloads. Alex: merging after CI. will push hotfix to prod in canary and monitor metrics. Ben: rolling hotfix to canary now. deploy-bot: deploy started at 2026-03-20T15:12:00Z. deploy-bot: canary up (2 instances). health OK. no errors in logs for preview during canary. Maya: after merge, please run the automated exploit suite against canary endpoint and verify WAF doesn't block sanitized responses. Eve: ran exploit suite vs canary — sanitized payloads are escaped, no script execution. responses still include the input but encoded. Priya: post-incident tasks (assign): - Alex: ship additional server-side validation + add integration test for preview route. - Daniel: complete log analysis and produce IOCs. - Maya: write internal postmortem draft. - Zoe: draft customer communication if needed. - Security: evaluate need for additional RBAC rules on preview creation. Alex: accepted. ETA for server-side validation and tests: EOD. Daniel: initial IOC list: requests from 54.173.22.11 with UA `Mozilla/5.0 (Scanner)`; query param patterns include `%3Cimg` and `onerror`. I'll upload IOC artifact to the incident ticket. Ben: keeping WAF rule active for 72h, then re-evaluate. Maya: retrospective items for postmortem: missing sanitization on client-only feature, lack of server-side validation, no unit tests for preview. also check audit log gaps for preview route. Priya: add KMS validation in the checklist for forensic storage and ensure key rotation policy applied. Zoe: will prepare a short customer note if Daniel finds evidence of targeted exploitation. otherwise internal-only. Maya: thanks everyone. will kick off the incident doc and assign tasks in INC-2026. closing thread as mitigation is active; followups tracked in the ticket. :white_check_mark:
